pin_title: A Handful of Quick Oats Disappears Into Thin Soup and Thickens It

pin_title: The Side Dish Should Do the Heavy Lifting, Not the Meat

pin_title: Six Eggs, Six Breakfast Burritos, Three Months in the Freezer
description: Six eggs across six burritos, plus a can of black beans and a cup of shredded cheese doing the rest of the work. These high protein breakfast burritos hold up for about 3 months in the freezer. Vegetarian, roughly 380 calories each, and no drive-thru involved.

pin_title: Frozen Breakfast Burrito: 2 Minutes, Flip, 1 to 2 More
description: Take the wrapping off, microwave 2 minutes, flip it, then go another 1 to 2 minutes. Don't thaw it in the fridge overnight and then microwave it, because the texture falls apart on that cycle. A breakfast burrito is only a good idea if reheating is this boring.
alt_text: Dark text pin reading straight from frozen, 2 minutes, flip, 1 to 2 more.

pin_title: Bake Breakfast Burritos 8 Minutes at 400F Before They See the Freezer
description: Seam side down, a sprinkle of cheese on top, 8 to 10 minutes at 400F. That bake sets the cheese and seals the tortilla edges, which is the difference between a high protein breakfast burrito and a soggy one. Cool completely, then wrap and freeze.
alt_text: Orange text pin reading bake the burritos 8 minutes at 400F before they see the freezer.

pin_title: 380 Calories a Breakfast Burrito, No Meat Anywhere In It
description: Eggs, black beans, corn, bell peppers, onion, cheese and salsa, rolled into 6 burritos at about 380 calories each. High protein breakfast ideas don't have to involve standing at a stove at 7 AM, because these come out of the freezer already built.
alt_text: Cream text pin reading 380 calories a breakfast burrito, no meat anywhere in it.

pin_title: 1 Cup of Oats, 2 Cups of Broth, and Breakfast Stops Being Sweet
description: Use a 1 to 2 ratio, oats to water or broth, and cook 5 to 7 minutes until it's thick and creamy. Savory oatmeal treats the grain like rice, something to hold your toppings instead of being the star. Broth is the single change that makes the whole bowl work.
alt_text: Cream text pin reading 1 cup of oats, 2 cups of broth, and breakfast stops being sweet.

pin_title: One Egg Adds About 6 Grams of Protein to Savory Oatmeal
description: The egg isn't decoration. About 6 grams of protein is what turns a bowl of savory oatmeal from a side dish into a breakfast that actually holds. Poached, soft fried, or scrambled, the yolk ends up as the sauce either way.
alt_text: Dark text pin reading one egg adds about 6 grams of protein, that is the difference.

pin_title: Poach the Egg 3 to 4 Minutes and Let the Yolk Be the Sauce
description: Drop a cracked egg into simmering water with a splash of vinegar for 3 to 4 minutes. The whites set, the yolk stays runny, and when you cut into it the yolk mixes straight through the savory oatmeal. No cream, no butter, no second pan.
alt_text: Orange text pin reading poach the egg 3 to 4 minutes and let the yolk be the sauce.

pin_title: Savory Oatmeal Keeps 4 Days in the Fridge
description: Cook it, cool it completely, and store it airtight for up to 4 days. Reheat a portion in the microwave with about 2 tablespoons of water and it loosens right back up. Savory oatmeal is the high protein breakfast that survives a real weekday.
alt_text: Cream text pin reading savory oatmeal keeps 4 days in the fridge, reheat with about 2 tablespoons of water.

pin_title: Breakfast Hash Timing: Vegetables 25 to 30 Minutes, Eggs 8 to 12
description: At 425F the sweet potatoes need twenty-five to thirty minutes to get good color, while eggs set in about eight to twelve. Roast the vegetables first, make wells, then crack the eggs in at the end. That timing is the entire breakfast hash.
alt_text: Cream text pin reading the vegetables need 25 to 30 minutes, the eggs need 8 to 12.

pin_title: Single Layer, With Gaps, or the Sweet Potatoes Just Steam
description: Four cups of sweet potato dumped onto one pan with no breathing room steams instead of roasting. You want a single layer with gaps between the pieces, even if that means splitting it across two pans. It's the difference between a crisp breakfast hash and a soft one.
alt_text: Dark text pin reading single layer with gaps, stack them and you made a casserole.

pin_title: A Half Sheet Pan Is 18 by 13 Inches, and This Breakfast Hash Assumes It
description: A standard half sheet pan measures 18 by 13 inches. If yours is a quarter sheet at roughly 9 by 13, split the breakfast hash across two pans or cook it in two rounds. Pan size decides whether you get crisp edges or steamed cubes.
alt_text: Orange text pin reading a half sheet pan is 18 by 13 inches, this recipe assumes it.

pin_title: Your Oven Needs 10 to 15 Minutes to Recover After You Open the Door
description: Most ovens take ten to fifteen minutes to fully come back up after the door opens. Slide a breakfast hash into a 425F oven that hasn't stabilized and every time in the recipe drifts. Give it the full preheat and stop wondering why the sweet potatoes are pale.
alt_text: Cream text pin reading your oven needs 10 to 15 minutes to recover after you open it.

pin_title: Put the Snack Bin at Eye Level. Visibility Is Half the Battle
description: A clear bin on the middle shelf beats the bottom crisper every time, because things go to the crisper to die. When you open the door it should be the first thing you see. That's the entire idea behind a grab and go snack drawer.
alt_text: Cream text pin reading put the snack bin at eye level, visibility is half the battle.

pin_title: If It Needs Washing or Peeling, It Doesn't Belong in the Snack Drawer
description: Everything in the bin has to be completely ready to eat. Whole unwashed carrots miss the point, because at four in the afternoon you're taking the path of least resistance every single time. Fill the snack drawer with things you can grab one handed.
alt_text: Dark text pin reading if it needs washing or peeling, it does not belong in the drawer.

pin_title: Restock the Snack Drawer 3 to 4 Days at a Time
description: Prep too far ahead and the cut produce dries out or turns slimy before anybody eats it. Twice a week keeps the snack drawer appealing instead of guilt inducing. Small batches, visible bin, done.
alt_text: Orange text pin reading restock the snack drawer 3 to 4 days at a time, not two weeks.

pin_title: Date the Hard-Boiled Eggs and Use Them Within One Week
description: Hard-boiled eggs anchor a good snack drawer, but they come with rules. Refrigerate within two hours of cooking, write the date on the container, and use them within one week. Keep the fridge at 40F or below and keep the bin away from any raw meat package that could leak.
alt_text: Cream text pin reading date the hard-boiled eggs and use them within one week.

pin_title: Three Cups of Air-Popped Popcorn Is About 90 Calories
description: If you want to eat a giant bowl of something in front of the TV, popcorn is the only logical pick. Three cups of air-popped runs about 90 calories, and the volume to calorie ratio is unbeatable. Chips give you four bites and a greasy hand.
alt_text: Cream text pin reading three cups of air-popped popcorn is about 90 calories.

pin_title: Slice Sweet Potatoes Paper Thin and Bake Them at 300 Degrees
description: Beets, sweet potatoes and parsnips make far better chips than the store-bought veggie versions. Slice them paper thin, toss with a tiny bit of oil, and go low at 300 degrees. You're basically dehydrating them, so it takes longer than you think.
alt_text: Dark text pin reading slice sweet potatoes paper thin and bake them at 300 degrees.

pin_title: At 3 PM Your Brain Wants Salty and Crunchy, Not a Lecture
description: You don't have to swear off potatoes forever to make a better call in the afternoon. Most of the time you just want a break and something salty to chew on while you stare at a screen. Popcorn, nuts and seeds, or thin vegetable chips all land in the same place.
alt_text: Orange text pin reading at 3 PM your brain wants salty and crunchy, not a lecture.

pin_title: Most Store-Bought Veggie Chips Are Potato Starch Dyed Green
description: Read the ingredients on a bag of veggie chips and it's usually potato starch with spinach powder for color. Slicing your own beets or parsnips takes a mandoline and a little patience, and it beats paying extra for the costume. Better snack, same crunch.
alt_text: Cream text pin reading most store-bought veggie chips are potato starch dyed green.

pin_title: 7 Popcorn Toppings That Don't Taste Like Diet Food
description: Lime zest with a pinch of heat, nutritional yeast with garlic, Parmesan and cracked pepper, sesame and nori, dill and onion, cocoa and cinnamon, and crushed freeze-dried berries. Seven ways to give plain popcorn a real personality without a syrup or a sauce.
alt_text: Cream text pin reading 7 popcorn toppings that do not taste like diet food.

pin_title: 8 Cups of Popcorn, 1 to 2 Teaspoons of Oil, 1 Tablespoon of Seasoning
description: For roughly 8 cups of popped popcorn, start with 1 to 2 teaspoons of oil and 1 tablespoon of dry seasoning. Toss, taste, and add another teaspoon or two only if the bowl asks for it. Parmesan and soy sauce powder bring their own salt, so taste first.
alt_text: Dark text pin reading 8 cups of popcorn, 1 to 2 teaspoons of oil, 1 tablespoon of seasoning.

pin_title: Cocoa Goes From Pleasantly Dark to Drywall Dust With Impressive Speed
description: Unsweetened cocoa with cinnamon and a small amount of sugar makes popcorn taste like a treat instead of a punishment. Add the cocoa gradually, because it turns on you fast. A pinch of salt makes the chocolate read clearer.
alt_text: Orange text pin reading cocoa goes from pleasantly dark to drywall dust with real speed.

pin_title: Whole Sesame Seeds Race to the Bottom of the Bowl. Crush Some First
description: Crush a sheet of nori into small flakes and mix it with toasted sesame seeds for a popcorn topping nobody expects. Whole seeds sink, so crush part of them and the mix actually clings. Soy sauce powder helps if you keep it around.
alt_text: Cream text pin reading whole sesame seeds race to the bottom of the bowl.

pin_title: Aim for 8 to 10 Grams of Fiber Before Noon
description: You don't need to hit the whole day's fiber at breakfast. Roughly 8 to 10 grams in the morning already puts you ahead of most muffin and latte routines. Stack any two easy high fiber breakfast foods and you're there before you've properly woken up.
alt_text: Cream text pin reading aim for 8 to 10 grams of fiber before noon.

pin_title: Oatmeal 4 Grams, a Spoon of Chia 5, a Cup of Raspberries 8
description: A cup of cooked oatmeal lands around 4 grams of fiber, a tablespoon of chia seeds adds about 5, and a cup of raspberries brings roughly 8. High fiber breakfast ideas are less about discovering weird ingredients and more about combining normal ones on purpose.
alt_text: Dark text pin listing oatmeal 4 grams, a spoon of chia 5, a cup of raspberries 8.

pin_title: Overnight Oats Can Clear 10 Grams of Fiber Before You Open Your Eyes
description: Oats, milk, chia and berries left in a jar overnight is often 10 plus grams of fiber before you're fully awake. The chia thickens it so it feels like pudding instead of cold porridge. Easiest high fiber breakfast on the list, and it makes itself.
alt_text: Orange text pin reading overnight oats can clear 10 grams of fiber before you wake up.

pin_title: Jumping From White Toast to 20 Grams of Fiber Is Why People Quit
description: If your current breakfast is mostly white toast, go slow. Going from almost no fiber to 20 grams before work is how people decide fiber doesn't agree with them. Add a bit more each week, drink water with it, and let a high fiber breakfast settle in.
alt_text: Cream text pin reading jumping from white toast to 20 grams of fiber is why people quit.

pin_title: Bread, Beans, Seeds: Three Levers That Make Avocado Toast a Real Meal
description: Bread with real whole grains near the top of the ingredient list, a topping that is not just salt, and something crunchy that isn't only there for the photo. That's high fiber avocado toast in three moves, at about 340 calories a serving.
alt_text: Cream text pin reading bread, beans, seeds, three levers make avocado toast a meal.

pin_title: Mashed Black Beans and Lime Turn Avocado Toast Into Actual Breakfast
description: Mash half a cup of rinsed black beans with a fork, spoon them over the avocado, and hit it with lime so it tastes bright instead of heavy. This is the avocado toast variation for people who want something closer to a meal than a snack.
alt_text: Dark text pin reading mashed black beans and lime turn avocado toast into breakfast.

pin_title: Spread Hummus Under the Avocado So the Toast Doesn't Go Soggy
description: A thin layer of hummus first, then avocado, cucumber slices and everything seasoning. It's the coolest of the avocado toast variations, which matters on mornings when hot food sounds like a bad idea. Assemble right before you eat it.
alt_text: Orange text pin reading spread hummus under the avocado so the toast stays crisp.

pin_title: A 5 Day Avocado Toast Rotation So You Stop Repeating Yourself
description: Beans and lime on Monday, tomatoes and seeds on Tuesday, hummus and cucumber on Wednesday, salsa and corn on Thursday, tahini and lemon zest on Friday. Same ten minutes every morning, five different high fiber breakfasts.
alt_text: Cream text pin reading a 5 day avocado toast rotation so you stop repeating yourself.

pin_title: 3 Tablespoons of Chia to 1 Cup of Liquid. That's the Ratio
description: The base for savory chia is 3 tablespoons of chia seeds to 1 cup of liquid. Broth or a savory milk base both work. It's the prep-ahead high fiber breakfast for people who are tired of sweet chia pudding and want something salty instead.
alt_text: Cream text pin reading 3 tablespoons of chia to 1 cup of liquid, that is the ratio.

pin_title: Stir Once, Wait 5 Minutes, Stir Again
description: That second stir is what saves you from a clump at the bottom that looks like it made a decision without you. Five minutes is the whole wait. Savory chia sets up smooth and stays that way through the week.
alt_text: Dark text pin reading stir once, wait 5 minutes, stir again, that second stir saves you.

pin_title: The Savory Chia Base Keeps About 4 Days in the Fridge
description: Make two or three jars at a time, because anything past that starts to feel like running a chia operation out of your refrigerator. The base holds about 4 days. Keep the toppings in a separate container so nothing goes soft on you.
alt_text: Orange text pin reading the savory chia base keeps about 4 days in the fridge.

pin_title: Pack the Toppings Separately. Nobody Wants Pressed Avocado at 7 AM
description: If you're taking savory chia to the office, keep the avocado, herbs and crunchy bits in their own container. Chia that's been pressed against avocado since 7 AM gets dramatic in the wrong direction. The toppings are what make it read as breakfast.

pin_title: USDA Puts One Adult at $303 to $381 a Month for Food at Home
description: The thrifty benchmark works out to about $303 a month for a woman living alone and $381 for a man, using May 2026 prices. That range already includes the 20 percent USDA adds for one person households. Use it as a shape to compare your own grocery spending against, not as a quote.

pin_title: Shopping for One Costs 20 Percent More Per Person, and USDA Priced It
description: USDA says to add 20 percent to the individual weekly cost for a one person household, 10 percent for two, and 5 percent for three. Smaller packages, more waste, and no way to buy the loss leader case. USDA priced the penalty, it didn't invent it.

pin_title: $73.20 a Week for a Man, $58.20 for a Woman, Then Add 20 Percent
description: USDA's May 2026 individual weekly costs are $73.20 for an adult man aged 20 to 50 and $58.20 for an adult woman in the same band. Add the one person 20 percent and you get $87.84 and $69.84 a week. That's where the monthly grocery number actually comes from.
alt_text: Orange text pin reading $73.20 a week for a man, $58.20 for a woman, then add 20 percent.

pin_title: That Grocery Benchmark Is Food at Home. Takeout Isn't In It
description: USDA's number covers food eaten at home. No restaurants, no delivery fees, no coffee bought because the morning went sideways. If your $400 includes three takeout meals, you're not overspending on groceries, you're spending on something else that happens to arrive on a plate.
alt_text: Cream text pin reading that grocery benchmark is food at home, takeout is not in it.

pin_title: USDA Says a Household of Four Can Eat at Home for $235 a Week
description: The Thrifty Food Plan puts the reference household of four at $235.00 a week and $1,018.20 a month, using May 2026 prices. That's $33.57 a day for the whole house. It's a benchmark USDA built, not a shopping list it wrote for you.
alt_text: Cream text pin reading USDA says a household of four can eat at home for $235 a week.

pin_title: $235 a Week Works Out to $8.39 Per Person Per Day
description: Divide USDA's weekly grocery benchmark across 4 people and 7 days and you land at about $8.39 per person per day. At three meals a day that averages roughly $2.80 a plate. It's an illustration, not an instruction to make every plate cost the same.
alt_text: Dark text pin reading $235 a week works out to $8.39 per person per day.

pin_title: USDA Doesn't Split the Grocery Money Into Four Equal Envelopes
description: The report assigns $73.20 a week to the adult man, $58.20 to the adult woman, $55.50 to the older child and $48.00 to the younger one. The displayed numbers add to $234.90 while USDA reports $235.00 from unrounded amounts. Ten cents of federal rounding, nobody is hiding anything.
alt_text: Orange text pin reading USDA does not split the grocery money into four equal envelopes.

pin_title: Add 20 Percent for One Person, 10 for Two, 5 for Three
description: USDA adjusts its grocery benchmark by household size: add 20 percent for one person, 10 percent for two, and 5 percent for three. Four gets no change, five or six subtract 5 percent, and seven or more subtract 10. That's how the thrifty table turns into your own shopping list.
alt_text: Cream text pin reading add 20 percent for one person, 10 for two, 5 for three.
board: Grocery Budget Tips and Shopping Lists

pin_title: Crusty Homemade Bread Lives on the Counter, Cut Side Down
description: A crackly crust and a plastic bag are enemies. For the first day or two, set the loaf cut side down on a wooden surface or in a paper bag and leave it alone. Storing homemade bread is mostly about matching the method to the crust you worked for.
alt_text: Cream text pin reading crusty homemade bread lives on the counter, cut side down.

pin_title: Soft Homemade Bread Keeps 3 to 4 Days in Airtight Storage
description: Airtight is right for a soft loaf, but only once the bread has cooled all the way through. Seal it warm and the trapped steam turns the crust gummy and invites mold early. Cool completely first, and homemade bread stretches to 3 or 4 good days.
alt_text: Dark text pin reading soft homemade bread keeps 3 to 4 days in airtight storage.

pin_title: Freeze Homemade Bread in Slices. They Go Straight in the Toaster
description: Slice before you freeze and future you takes out exactly what the morning needs. Frozen slices go straight into the toaster, or thaw at room temperature in about 20 to 30 minutes. It beats watching half a loaf of homemade bread go stale on the counter.
alt_text: Orange text pin reading freeze homemade bread in slices, they go straight in the toaster.
board: Sourdough Discard Recipes and Easy Bread

pin_title: A 300F Oven for 5 to 10 Minutes Brings a Stale Loaf Back, Briefly
description: Stale is dry and leathery, and it's fixable. Mist the crust lightly with water and warm the loaf at 300F for 5 to 10 minutes. It won't be the hour it left the oven, but it beats the alternative, and stale homemade bread still becomes toast, croutons or breadcrumbs.
alt_text: Cream text pin reading a 300F oven for 5 to 10 minutes brings a stale loaf back.

pin_title: One Cup of Sourdough Discard Is About 227 Grams

pin_title: Half a Cup of Sourdough Discard Is About 113 Grams
description: 113 grams comes straight out of the 227 gram cup. If you've seen 120 or 125 grams somewhere else, that recipe is using a different house conversion or a denser starter. Don't average five websites together like you're setting an interest rate.

pin_title: Put the Bowl on the Scale, Hit Tare, and Skip the Sticky Cup
description: Set the mixing bowl on a digital scale, press tare, and spoon sourdough discard in until you hit the number in the recipe. Overshoot by 4 or 5 grams and pancakes will forgive you. For a dough where hydration matters, get closer to the target.
alt_text: Orange text pin reading put the bowl on the scale, hit tare, skip the sticky cup.

pin_title: Sourdough Discard: 1 Cup Is 227g, Half a Cup Is 113g, a Quarter Cup Is 57g
description: Three numbers cover almost every sourdough discard recipe you'll open: 227 grams a cup, 113 grams a half cup, 57 grams a quarter cup. Write them on a piece of tape near your scale and stop looking them up at 8 AM with flour on your hands.
alt_text: Cream text pin listing 1 cup equals 227g, half a cup 113g, a quarter cup 57g of sourdough discard.

pin_title: How to Cook Chicken Breast: Four to Six Minutes a Side, Pulled at 165F
description: The best way to cook chicken breast in a skillet is four to six minutes per side over real heat, pulled at an internal temperature of 165F. pin_title: How to Cook Chicken Breast Without Drying It Out: Even Cutlets
description: A thin edge overcooks while a thick center is still climbing to 165F, and that's most dry chicken right there. Slice the breast horizontally into even cutlets first. The best way to cook chicken is salt, heat and a thermometer, not an overnight marinade pretending Tuesday started yesterday.
alt_text: Dark text pin reading even cutlets solve more than a complicated marinade ever will.

pin_title: A 12-Inch Skillet Holds Four Thin Cutlets, and Not One More
description: Crowding traps steam, drops the pan temperature, and leaves you with pale chicken sitting in a puddle. Cook in two batches and keep the first loosely covered on a plate. Everybody learning how to cook chicken in a skillet gets this wrong exactly once.
alt_text: Orange text pin reading a 12-inch skillet holds four thin cutlets, and not one more.

pin_title: Rest the Chicken 5 Minutes or the Juice Ends Up on the Board
description: Take the chicken out of the pan and let it sit at least 5 minutes before slicing. Cut too soon and more juice runs onto the board than stays in the meat. Then scrape up the browned bits with a squeeze of lemon and a teaspoon of Dijon, and the best way to cook chicken comes with a sauce attached.
alt_text: Cream text pin reading rest the chicken 5 minutes or the juice ends up on the board.

pin_title: Pull Pork Chops at 145F and Rest Them 5 to 10 Minutes
description: 145F is USDA's safe minimum for whole pork chops, followed by at least a 3 minute rest. This method rests them 5 to 10, which is where the juice settles back in. Don't pull at 135F and assume optimism will supply the missing temperature.
alt_text: Cream text pin reading pull pork chops at 145F and rest them 5 to 10 minutes.

pin_title: Bone-In Pork Chops About 1 Inch Thick Are the Ones That Survive a Skillet
description: The bone insulates the meat so it cooks more evenly, and good marbling keeps it from drying out. Thin chops are much harder to cook without overdoing them. If you want to know the best way to cook pork chops, the answer starts at the meat counter.
alt_text: Dark text pin reading bone-in pork chops about 1 inch thick are the ones that survive.
board: How to Cook Chicken, Pork and Beef

pin_title: Butter Basting Pork Chops Is 2 to 3 Minutes of Spooning
description: Sear first, then drop in butter with garlic and herbs and spoon it over the pork chops for another 2 to 3 minutes while you watch the thermometer. If the garlic burns, you added it too early. It belongs in the lower heat basting stage, not the sear.

pin_title: Pork Chops Thicker Than 1 1/4 Inches Need a 375F Oven Finish
description: Sear both sides, add the aromatics, then move an oven safe skillet into a 375F oven until the center reaches 145F. That's cleaner than burning the garlic while a thick center negotiates with the stove. Thin and boneless chops go the other way and finish faster.

pin_title: The Cabbage Slaw Is the Whole Point of a Fish Taco
description: Mayonnaise, lime juice and a minced chipotle in adobo, tossed through two cups of shredded cabbage. That homemade dressing is what makes a fish taco feel like a full plate instead of fish in a tortilla. Make the slaw first and let it sit.
alt_text: Cream text pin reading the cabbage slaw is the whole point, the fish is incidental.

pin_title: Let the Cabbage Slaw Sit 15 Minutes. It Only Gets Better
description: Salt the shredded cabbage while you mix the dressing, then let the whole bowl sit at least 15 minutes. The dressing softens it just enough that you're not crunching through your teeth, and it holds fine if you make the slaw hours ahead.
alt_text: Dark text pin reading let the slaw sit 15 minutes, it only gets better.

pin_title: Fish Tacos With Cabbage Slaw in 20 Minutes, No Fryer
description: A pound of mild white fish seared 2 to 3 minutes a side, warm corn tortillas, and the chipotle cabbage slaw doing the heavy lifting. Four servings at about 340 calories each, and nothing touched a deep fryer or six napkins.
alt_text: Orange text pin reading fish tacos in 20 minutes, no fryer, about 340 calories.

pin_title: Red Cabbage Works Fine in a Slaw. It Also Turns Everything Purple
description: Half a small head gets you the two cups you need. Don't stress about perfect shreds, because a mix of thin ribbons and chunkier pieces gives better texture. Red cabbage tastes the same in the slaw and turns it a color you should probably expect.
alt_text: Cream text pin reading red cabbage works fine, it also turns the slaw purple.

pin_title: Boil, Smash, Roast at 425F: Potato Salad With Actual Crunch
description: Simmer baby potatoes 15 to 20 minutes, smash them flat on an oiled pan, then roast 20 to 25 minutes at 425F until the jagged edges are crisp. This potato salad is a full departure from the cold deli tub version everybody ignores at the barbecue.
alt_text: Cream text pin reading boil, smash, roast at 425F, potato salad with actual crunch.

pin_title: Toss the Potatoes in Dijon Vinaigrette While They're Still Warm
description: Warm potatoes act like sponges, so they pull in the homemade dressing instead of just wearing it. Whisk olive oil, apple cider vinegar, Dijon, a little honey and minced shallot, then fold it through with parsley and chives. Vinaigrette beats mayonnaise in a potato salad every time.
alt_text: Dark text pin reading toss the potatoes in the Dijon vinaigrette while still warm.

pin_title: Potato Salad at a Potluck: Two Hours Out, One Hour Above 90 Degrees
description: A vinaigrette doesn't make cooked potatoes shelf stable. Keep the bowl refrigerated until you serve, then get it back into a cooler within two hours, or one hour when it's above 90 degrees F outside. A larger bowl of ice underneath buys you time.
alt_text: Orange text pin reading potato salad at a potluck, two hours out, one above 90 degrees.

pin_title: 220 Calories a Serving of Potato Salad, and Not One Spoonful of Mayonnaise
description: A pound and a half of baby potatoes makes six servings at about 220 calories each. The Dijon and vinegar dressing brings acid, which is exactly what heavy starchy food needs. It's the potato salad people actually come back to for seconds.
alt_text: Cream text pin reading 220 calories a serving and not one spoonful of mayonnaise.
